title: Sotol Creek Family Dental — a before/after website makeover
description: A before/after makeover for an invented north San Antonio family dental practice. The 2011 site has pale-blue 11 px text on blue, a "Skip Intro" bar, an image-only phone number and services list, an 8.1 MB hero (simulated), "PAINLESS DENTISTRY GUARANTEED!" and no hours. The friendly, mobile-first rebuild has a clear 'Book a visit' action, tap-to-call, early and Saturday hours with a live open/closed badge in US Central time, plain service descriptions with no medical claims, a booking request form, sample reviews marked as such, an FAQ and Dentist JSON-LD. There's a 'What changed' panel, and 11 in-page checks (not Lighthouse) score both versions.
prompt: Make a before/after website makeover for a fictional San Antonio family dental practice as proof for my $1,200 Landing Page, Built + Tested package. No medical claims beyond ordinary service descriptions. The before should be a believable dated site: tiny low-contrast text, no clear call to action, the phone number and services as images without alt text, a slow huge hero (simulated), no hours, no meta description and no mobile layout, in a scaled frame so the page never scrolls sideways. The after should be modern, accessible and mobile-first, with tap-to-call, hours with open/closed-now in Central time via Intl, a map-free location block, a booking CTA, sample reviews that are labelled as samples, an FAQ and Dentist JSON-LD. Add a keyboard-accessible before/after toggle, a 'What changed' panel linked to highlighted areas, a live in-page scorecard that is clearly not Lighthouse, a CTA to my services section and a footer that says it's fictional.

methodology: Independent oracle for the scorecard: the spec reads raw computed styles, rects and head tags from each frame and judges all 11 checks in Node with its own WCAG luminance code. It compares every pass flag and count with the page's data attributes, for both versions and both preview widths, and again after the booking form adds its status line.
Contrast reference values first (21:1, 4.54:1 for #767676 on white, #777777 just under 4.5), then every text element of the rebuild, FAQ answers opened, must pass AA.

Hours under page.clock with a noon close and a short Friday: the 1 PM Friday close in daylight time is checked in contexts set to Pacific/Kiritimati and America/Los_Angeles. The 8 AM Saturday opening ('until noon'), Saturday afternoon ('opens Monday at 7:30 AM'), Sunday and a 5 PM weekday close are checked in standard time, against the test's own table and the published US DST offsets.

Health-copy assertions: the rebuild's text must not match painless, guarantee, perfect smile, cure or best dentist. The footer must say the descriptions are not medical advice, and the booking form must ask people not to include health details. The old site's 'PAINLESS DENTISTRY GUARANTEED' line is what the 'What changed' claims fix highlights.

Dentist JSON-LD must parse, match the tel: links and match the hours table day by day, with no rating markup. Also checked: keyboard tabs, 'What changed' highlighting and scrolling, no horizontal overflow at 360 px, and no network requests from the form.
risks: 'No medical claims' is enforced by a word list, and a claim in words the list doesn't include would get through. The list reflects this page's copy, not a general standard.
The Saturday 'until noon' wording depends on a noon special case in both the page and the test. Hours ending at 12:30 PM would read '12:30 PM', which is intended.
Contrast is judged against background-color only, so a future hero photo behind text would be misjudged. The rebuild keeps text on solid fills.

The page and the oracle choose text elements the same way, so a shared definition error wouldn't show up. A deliberate threshold change that moved elements across the line was caught when tried on the sibling taqueria page.
qa.playwright: This shares its structure with the other two makeovers. The spec reads the srcdoc frames with frameLocator and an evaluate on contentDocument, and page.clock.install + pauseAt + runFor(61 s) crosses each boundary exactly. setSystemTime doesn't fire timers, so each jump is followed by a minute's runFor, and every case was chosen to hold for that whole minute. getByLabel inside the frame worked for the fieldset of radio buttons ('Returning'), which confirms the labels are wired up and not just placed nearby. browser.newContext({ timezoneId }) checks one instant under two machine zones. There are no screenshot assertions, so visual polish is unverified.
coverage: Scorecard vs independent oracle, both versions, both preview widths
WCAG AA contrast of the whole rebuild, formula reference values
Dentist JSON-LD vs visible phone and hours
Hours across CDT and CST boundaries: Friday 1 PM, Saturday noon, Sunday, weekday
No medical promises, 'not medical advice', no health details on the form, services only as an image before
Tap-to-call, keyboard tabs, no horizontal scroll at 360 px, 'What changed' highlights, services CTA and fiction labels

a11y: The toggle is a WAI-ARIA tablist with a roving tabindex and Arrow, Home and End keys. The hidden frame is inert. Frames have descriptive titles, fix buttons name the fix they show, and changes are announced through aria-live. The scorecard is a table with headers. In the rebuild, the fields have visible labels, the radio buttons sit in a fieldset with a legend and are 24 px, the map has a text alternative, and all text passes WCAG AA by the page's own check.
